items.title: Lure of the Championship - Why foreign coaches are drawn to England's second tier
items.excerpt: The focus is often on the lack of opportunities for British coaches but look at it another way and it is remarkable that 16 of the clubs in the sixth-richest league in European football – two thirds of them – are currently being coached by…
body: The focus is often on the lack of opportunities for British coaches but look at it another way and it is remarkable that 16 of the clubs in the sixth-richest league in European football – two thirds of them – are currently being coached by men from the British Isles.

This is the famous Championship, offering raucous crowds, potential riches and a route to the Premier League. That is what has drawn the other eight - coaches from Belgium, Italy, France, Germany, Sweden, Switzerland and two from Portugal - with more waiting.

Each of these men are first-time managers in English football and while not all of them will find success here, the odds are in favour of at least one of them being able to call themselves a Premier League manager once the Championship season is concluded.

Top coaches are alive to the possibilities in England's second tier. It was a privilege to attend two games with Portuguese coach Vitor Campelos recently to gain a greater appreciation not just of the game here but its appeal to those working elsewhere.

items.title: Poch open to Man Utd talks with Carrick's position increasingly in doubt
items.excerpt: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, with Mauricio Pochettino open to a discussion if he were approached by the club.
body: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, with Mauricio Pochettino open to a discussion if he were approached by the club.

CEO Omar Berrada and Wilcox are due to meet minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco for a scheduled meeting on Wednesday, with the duo to discuss the findings of their season review and give their recommendations on Carrick's future, while also assessing their options.
Sky Sports News has been told that, as yet, no final decision has been taken on Carrick's Old Trafford future.
With Pochettino open to talks with United, it is thought the cost of buying him out of his contract with his current job as USA head coach would be around £7m.

body: Xaver Schlager has been quietly impressive for Nottingham Forest this season but what was missing was that big moment. It came in the 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday when he dispossessed Elliot Anderson for Liam Delap's first goal.

The free transfer from Leipzig nipped in ahead of the £116m man that he has replaced in Forest's midfield and set Delap on the way to doubling the lead. Schlager is no Anderson but he has his own qualities and they made the difference at the weekend.

items.title: Carrick position increasingly in doubt as hierarchy mulls over his future
items.excerpt: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, but Sky Sports News has been told as yet, no final decision has been taken about his future.
items.byline: Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett and Danyal Khan
body: Michael Carrick's position as Manchester United head coach is looking increasingly in doubt, but Sky Sports News has been told as yet, no final decision has been taken about his future.

As reported earlier on Monday, the club is carrying out a full review of the team's performance so far this season, led by director of football Jason Wilcox, with a plan for a decision to be made before the end of this international break.
Carrick was given a reprieve following the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago, with the bosses keen to give him a further three matches to try to turn the team's fortunes around.

But the pressure has continued to mount on Carrick after an eighth straight Premier League match without a win. There are now real doubts about whether he will be in charge of the team which goes to Anfield to play Liverpool the weekend after next.

items.title: Ballon d'Or winner Kane not named in FIFPRO World 11
items.excerpt: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has not been named in the FIFPRO World 11.
body: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane has not been named in the FIFPRO World 11.
Over 18,000 professional footballers have chosen their best men's team, with the final 11 being chosen from a group of 26 selected finalists.
Kane, who won the Ballon d'Or ahead of Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe by one of the smallest margins in history, was among the 26 finalists but did not make the final team.
Mbappe, Manchester City's Erling Haaland, Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Inter Miami's Lionel Messi were named in a Kane-less front four, which also excluded Cristiano Ronaldo and Michael Olise.

Carrick and the players have all had Monday off after rescuing a late point against Villa on Sunday, but the head coach and his staff are due back into Carrington on Tuesday.

items.excerpt: Welcome to The Euro Debrief , the Sky Sports column in which Adam Bate rounds up some of the key stories from the latest matches across the continent. This week: Kane is the assist king Barcelona win in Madrid Inter close gap on Lazio Eleve…

This week: Kane is the assist king Barcelona win in Madrid Inter close gap on Lazio Eleven in a row for PSG Weghorst denies Ajax Bundesliga: Kane is assist king

Whisper it but Harry Kane has gone four games without scoring a goal. That has only happened once before in his Bayern Munich career and in that sequence he went off at half-time in one game and came on as a second-half substitute in another. Drought!

It is not an issue for Kane or club because the England captain laid on both goals for his team-mates in a 2-1 win at Mainz that maintains Bayern's place at the top of the Bundesliga table. The Ballon d'Or winner has become the competition's king of assists this season.

His square pass set up the first for Joshua Kimmich and his lay-off left Lennart Karl with the simplest of tasks for the second. Following on from his lofted assist for Konrad Laimer to score against Atletico Madrid in midweek, it is a growing element of Kane's game.
